_comment: Insight nodes for NPC name reveals. Per the locked doctrine (see docs/design/insight_revelation_system.md *Implementation status*), the name reveal fires on the ACT that proves the NPC is what they are -- not the first dialog open. For the Guide, that act is the Signing: him doing the thing he was sent to do is the moment the Vagrant understands 'this is the Guide.' The HP-bar / dialog speaker flip to 'Guide' the same frame the picker closes.

knows_guide._comment: Fires on signing_committed. The Signing IS the guidance -- naming happens through act, not interaction. Before commit, he is a stranger with words.

knows_lupa_felled._comment: Observation. Fires when the large wolf-like creature on the slope falls. Operational voice: he saw a beast die. No 'Lupa', no 'apex predator', no Italian -- those are reveals he hasn't earned. Pairs with knows_guide_poisoned_carcass to support concludes_guide_killed_lupa.

knows_guide_poisoned_carcass._comment: Observation. Fires when the player advances through the Guide's first_meeting_b dialog beat (where the Guide confesses he poisoned the carcass Lupa was feeding from). Triggered by an on_select hook on the Continue. choice in that topic that sets the gating flag. Operational voice: the man at the chapel says he poisoned the food the beast was eating. The Vagrant has heard a claim; he hasn't connected it to the beast's death yet -- that's the conclusion.

infers_meat_state._comment: Inference (cognition-system v1 simplified). Player picks one of three interpretations of what happened to the beast. Warrant is per-inference (does the player have linked evidence at all), not per-reading. WHO laid the poison lives on a separate downstream inference.

readings.text: The meat was rotten. The beast ate what it should not have eaten and sickened from it. Such is how the wild ends -- a careless meal, a slow turning of the body against itself.
Something was wrong with the flesh. Dark streaks within, a sweetness in the air that does not belong. Someone or something laid death into the meat the beast was eating.

The meat the beast was eating was poisoned. Dark streaks within the flesh, a sweetness in the air that does not belong to honest rot. The beast ate. The beast died. Who laid the poison there, and to what end, I cannot yet say.
